probe.note: live_window is set to 10 years so the recorded sessions count as recently active regardless of when the fixture was checked out. self_session is set to the name-collision session so the guard for the Doctor's own session is exercised separately from the collision guard.

findings.why: The static layer reports the same file from its own angle: it sits inside the search path in a shape the loader does not read. The active-runtime layer adds that a running session still has it. Both are true and neither replaces the other.

The session's startup skill set lists "moved-away" and the file is still inside the search path but in a shape the loader does not read. The description recorded for the session matches the file's declared description, so they are the same capability. A configuration change reaches a session only when it starts.
The always-loaded rule's mtime is after this session started, so the session holds the earlier text. Only timestamps were compared: claude-code session records do not store instruction text.
Timestamps are compared even for a non-interactive session: restricted launch flags change which capabilities it has, not when it started.

no_findings.name: still-there
no_findings.why: Present in the session and still discovered. Same name, same state, nothing stale.
This is the Doctor's own session in this fixture. Divergence there is expected and must never be reported.
The non-interactive session also lists moved-away, but its capability set is not compared: restricted launch flags make a difference from the configured state expected.
